There is no placement of the root mantra (mūlamantra-nyāsa). The worship: Hrauṃ, obeisance to the one whose hand has transcended peace and quiescence (śānti-śāntyatīta-kara).
32a) To the ear: *Hraiṃ*, homage to Śāntikalā. *Lugotrasa*.
Hrūṃ, obeisance to Vidyākalā. ...........?
Hrīṃ, salutation to the digit of establishment (Pratiṣṭhākalā). [Salutation] to the Liṅga.
Hrāṃ, salutation to Nivṛttikalā. Cchugoḍasa.
Worship in forward and reverse order; worship with the six limbs.
The swift, honey-colored steed has been yoked. Gāyatrī.
Oṃ, let us know Paśupati; let us meditate upon Viśvakarman; may he impel our life-force.
At the time of the *samaya*, [the practitioner] should hold the *argha* vessel with both hands doubled over.
The *kegola* [is] like a *khajoḍha* [or] *avataya*. From today onwards, in the sentence.
O Goddess of gods, I have seized this animal as a vow-offering with a devoted heart;
grant to him also the attainment of heaven and the fortune of spiritual success.
Like one who has attained the state of a great festival: "Utphullām" and so forth.
One should not use the weapon-mantra for the vessel of offering water.
32b) In the wheel of the request for the cutting of auspiciousness; in the wheel fixed by *tha-ma-jo-ḍha*; the shadow of auspiciousness (*śivacchāyā*).
The shadow of the moment; the departure of the moment; the passing away of the moment.
For the purpose of libation: "The satisfied departed spirits," and so forth, in the mantra. [Insert] the three *bindus*. 3. One should recite the *samayabhojya* (the pledge-food).
The shadow of the *kaliṅka* tree. O King, blessings!

I bow to the venerable Śrīvāmā, who is of a single form yet manifold, the sovereign lady who fills the three worlds; she is the mistress of the Vasus and the lord of beings in the east, equal to the sky in the north, the divine mistress of the night in the south; she is the mistress of Kuja inaccessible to ordinary knowledge, the leader of the Kula-gaṇas, and the destroyer of the darkness of the western quarter.
The Mother of All Beings shall reveal [herself]. She is the bestower of success. For the sake of the southern path. By means of recitation.
One may perform the *mohanī* [rite] with the body alone according to one's desire; first, the *ucchuya*.
Self-blessing.
O Mother, the first stage is the Blessed One, whose nature is consciousness; then follow those abounding in knowledge and will—Hari, Hara, and Brahmā, the triad of rays;
then the five radiant Bhairavas, and thereafter the five venerable Yoginīs.
May the sixfold group consisting of Candra, Arka, Camarī, Amala, Mā, and Nitya, along with Kuja, protect me always.
The sacrificer and the others, having entered the enclosure, [performed] the Svāhākāra.
For the sake of recitation, for the sake of painting, for the sake of erasure. For the sake of delusion, for the sake of painting, for the sake of erasure.
The letter *ū* is the origin of wind and so forth; "ceta" refers to sandalwood (*śrīkhaṇḍa*) and the like.
Sidhara || Vīreśvarī, Mahāvīrā, and so forth || Mohinī ||

She who deludes the three worlds, who burns the hosts of enemies, who shatters all obstacles, who removes the fear and suffering caused by *bhūtas*, *pretas*, and *piśācas*, who destroys the *ḍākinīs*,
who is the protector of men, who is endowed with Śiva and all his powers, and who is possessed of every auspiciousness— that Goddess is the Enchantress (*Mohanīyā*).
Possessing the movement of the triple path, she bestows the life-force of all truth.
33b) By way of being well-bathed: "Utphullāntyādi" (beginning with "Utphullā"), [and] "Svānamālakostāviya."
For the purpose of dismissing [the deities] with the weapon-mantra and the offering: Nośiya, Valibho, Kaluya, Sākṣithāya.
Thus ends the ritual manual for the worship of the wheel of the illustrious Śrī-Śrī-Śrī-Siddhilakṣmī.
Now, the hymn of praise.
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed—the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which all that is moving and unmoving is pervaded. || 1 ||
To the illustrious Mahābhairava. The Illustrious Goddess said:
Within the mandala of the venerable Samvarta, the power of bliss is established through the stages of the Krama; it is most formidable.
According to the principle of emanation, there is a group of four belonging to both Akula and Kula, another group of five, and another group of six.
There are four, another five, and again four; this is the sixteenfold consecration of the Command (ājñā).
The divine eight are within the liberation: Ha, Sa, Kha, Pha, La, Ka, the digit (kalā), the flower-point (vindupuṣpa), and the space-seal (khamudrā). || 2 ||

The goddesses of the wheel of the digits of Supreme Śiva [worship] Vālaṃko Mālavṛddha; the essence of the divisions of the couple is the venerable Nātha, newly manifested in Candrapūrī. In the first Kali age, there were three descents of the Siddhas, and their authority was established in Koṅkaṇa.
Indeed, their sons and disciples are nine persons in number; among them, there are sixteen.

The lineage is the mass of the *gotra*, complete with the sequence of steps and sixteen rays, ending with the *krama*; these are indeed the remaining mandalas, pure through their circumambulation, increased by the reality of what is to be worshipped.
From the beginning to the end of eighteen, it is the entirety of the family lineage (*kulakrama*), preceded by the station of the mandala.
Having offered the refuse as a sacrificial animal through the threefold transference, there is the purification of the body in the fire of Śiva, which effects the destruction of impurities.
Bow down to that best of gurus, Śrī Kujeśa Bhairava, by whom the intermediate ground of rest, expansion, experience, conviction, and one’s own authority have been brought into union. || 4 ||
34b) Oṃ, homage to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī!
Aiṃ! Salutations to you, O Great Illusion (Mahāmāyā), who have transcended the body and are stainless;
O Pratyaṅgirā, Mother of the World, O Rājalakṣmī, salutations to you! || 5 ||
Varṇadehā Mahāgaurī is set in motion by the will of the practitioner;
Padadehā Mahāsphālā has arisen from great supernatural power (mahāsiddhi).
In that state, the Goddess residing within the body is remembered as the one who bestows grace upon practitioners;
she is Mahākuṇḍalinī, who pierces through and breaks open the thousand-petalled lotus.
Situated between the iḍā and piṅgalā, she is the sky-like one who has become wind;
having the form of a lotus fiber, she moves within the center of the suṣumnā.
Established in sound through the end of sound, they are beyond sound and free from passion;
they abide in the subtle, the gross, and the extremely subtle, within an inconceivable form.
In the supreme Śiva, who is beyond the highest and the lower, merged in Brahman,
whose form and conduct are inconceivable, she bestows the fruit of inconceivable goals.
The Mother of the Universe dwelling alone, residing in Karavīra;
she is the eternal bestower of the Great Throb, the one who effects the Great Convergence. 11.
The Goddess resides in the center of the *bindu*, curved like a crescent moon;
she whose abode is the *dvādaśānta* dwells in the sixteen supports.
Intermingled with cause and effect, situated in the middle of the channel of consciousness,
she is established in nine ways within the great wheel at the root of power (śaktimūla).
The supreme goddess is bodiless, yet within the body she takes the form of vital breath;
her nature is like the flow of nectar, and her supreme form is the syllable Om.
The Goddess resembles a flash of lightning, free from existence and non-existence;
she dwells eternally within the lotus of the heart, the Supreme Mistress whose form is peace. 15.
Consisting of the three natures— sattva, rajas,
and tamas— you alone, O Goddess, are the giver of life to all beings.
By you alone is the universe created; abiding in manifold ways through your divine play, you are the supreme goddess Mālinī, who binds even the cremation ground. 17.
O Cakrasundarī, who pierces the *hattālu* and revolves the wheels, who pervades the divine through the obstruction of the door of the *bindu*, salutations be to you! 18.
Resembling ten million suns, exceedingly pure like ten million moons, possessing the loveliness of ten million Kandarpas, and having the cosmic egg as his body. (19)
O Great Illusion, who art without space, without appearance, without stain, and without form; O Thou called Sakala, who grantest boons and art worshipped by the Asuras! 20.
The female mouse (dundarī) is situated between the letter *e* within the fire located at the letters *kha* and *pha*,
amidst the groups of letters ending in the letter *m*, within the auspicious (*śiva*) five-fold aggregate.
In the view that the form is crooked like a serpent and is supreme in the power of sound (nāda-śakti), Jālandharī is the eternal one residing in the wheel of the bindu (bindu-cakra). || 22 ||
Seated upon a vast throne of lapis lazuli, established in Pūrṇapīṭha, abiding in Kāma, transcending all parts (kalās), known as Kāmākhya, and born from the Bhaga. || 23 ||
She is the Brahma-knot in the swelling of the Kalās, flowing through the central channel;
she is Śivā, omnipresent and subtle, the great festival of eternal bliss. (24)
O leader of mantras, knower of mantras, dwelling within the treasury of knowledge;
O sovereign of Meru, moving through the night, situated in the midst of the five seats! 25.
She is indeed Khecarī and Bhūcarī, flowing with the three powers;
she has arisen from the fire at the end of time, and she is the one who brings an end to even the Destroyer of Time.
Within the twelve mandalas of the Kāli cycle related to the Kālikākrama, there is the goddess who consumes the three worlds; she is the thirteenth form.
In the Great Sequence (Mahākrama), which is called the Inexplicable (Anākhyā), there are creation, maintenance, and withdrawal;
[therein dwell] Bhāsā, known as Guhyakālī, and Nirvāṇeśī, the Supreme Sovereign.
Jhaṃkāriṇī, Bhairavī, Svarṇakoṭeśvarī, Śivā, Rājarājeśvarī, Caṇḍā, Aghoreśī, and Niśeśvarī. (29)
Sundarī, Tripurā, Padmā, Tārā, Pūrṇeśvarī,
Jayā, Kuvjikā, and Ambikā— the Mistress of the Krama— reside in the center of the Krama-maṇḍala.
Through the distinction between the elder and the younger, she is known as Kuvja and Ugracaṇḍikā;
she is Brahmāṇī, Raudrī, Kaumārī, and Vaiṣṇavī with a long nose. (31)
One should worship Vajriṇī, Carcikā, and Lakṣmī as the divine Mothers;
and [the Lords of the Yoginīs] known as Asitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodheśa, and Unmatta.
Kapālī, the one named Bhīṣaṇa, and Saṃhāra as the eighth—grant prosperity and perfection to your devotees and practitioners. (33)
The great goddess Siddhilakṣmī is proclaimed by Bhairava;
she shatters all the activities of those who hate the practitioner.
Homage to you, O Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, the performer of reversals;
O Ḍākinī, who devours all, such as Kāla, the planets, spirits, and the like. (35)
The Goddess protects the practitioner; we bow to Kālasaṃkarṣaṇī.
The Goddess bestows auspiciousness and protects the world with ease. (36)

I bow to the Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, who bestows the attainment of sovereignty, who is worthy of protection, who is affectionate toward her devotees, for the sake of accomplishing inconceivable goals. (37)
I pay homage to Pratyaṅgirā, who crushes all enemies, destroys misfortune and afflictions, and brings about the accomplishment of inconceivable goals. (38)
I bow to Pratyaṅgirā, the boat for crossing the ocean of calamities, the supreme bestower of nirvāṇa, the fortune of accomplishment, and the granter of victory. (39)
I bow to Pratyaṅgirā, who bestows sovereignty, wealth, and fortune; who grants liberation, destroys suffering, is the very embodiment of the fortune of accomplishment, and bestows victory. (40)
She who pacifies wicked enemies, destroys great diseases, is the fortune that grants the accomplishment of *pratyaṅgirā*, and bestows victory. || 41 ||
I bow to Pratyaṅgirā, who pacifies the evil dreams of the Kali age, destroys great sins, is the very embodiment of the fortune of success, and bestows victory. 42.
I meditate upon the goddess Pratyaṅgirā, who bestows inconceivable success, who grants the power of one's desired objects, who is the fortune of accomplishment, and who grants victory. 43.
I bow to Pratyaṅgirā, who pacifies royal calamities, destroys the afflictions of death, is the very fortune of accomplishment, and bestows victory. 44.
I bow to Pratyaṅgirā, the mother of kings, the royal fortune who bestows the supreme fruit of sovereignty, the goddess of success, and the granter of victory.
The Great Vidyā Siddhilakṣmī, the bestower of great accomplishments, [should be worshipped]; one should either recite or cause others to recite this hymn named Pratyaṅgirā. (46)
By reciting it, one may paralyze and crush enemy armies in an instant;
even the unthought-of are accomplished, and through recitation, one attains perfection.
It pacifies great faults, destroys great diseases, and eliminates the fear of lions, tigers, and malevolent planets, as well as the calamities caused by kings. || 48 ||
O Goddess, this great hymn, which brings peace and destroys the afflictions of the planets as well as those caused by water and fire, shall be recited by practitioners at the time of worship. (49)
For them, there is no accomplishment that does not exist, which bestows satisfaction upon the Goddess; there is nothing that cannot be achieved within the Kaulika teaching of the Kula.
Whatever desire one contemplates, that is accomplished effortlessly;
this is the truth, the absolute truth, O Great Goddess—there is nothing equal to this Kaulika [teaching]. 38b) 51.
Rising at midnight and lighting a lamp in the night,
if this hymn is recited, everything one has intended shall be accomplished.
Without the preliminary ritual (puraścaryā), one attains success through the recitation of this hymn;
the ascetic should recite it before a mandala, before an image, or before a mandala. 53.
This great hymn has been proclaimed as the bestower of the accomplishment of inconceivable aims;
it must never be given to those who are devoted to other deities. 54.
It should be given to one endowed with devotion and who delights in the family initiation (kuladīkṣā);
otherwise, they fall—such is the command of the Supreme Lord.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, the hymn to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī Mahāmāyā, brought down by the venerable Siddhinātha from the Tridaśaḍāmara Kānavīra.
I ever revere the Lord of the Field (Kṣetreśvara), who has become the pillar for all Kaulikas, who wears a garland of the hosts of hell-wardens,
and who stands at the gateway with a skull-topped staff, a sword, a choice bell, and a *kādi* in his hands.
Of her who is the beloved of the Lord of the Three Worlds. || 56 ||
May Skanda, renowned in the illustrious teaching as Vaṭukanātha, the smoke-bannered one who consumes the forest of the hosts of enemies,
the son of Gaurī, bearing a blazing spear, clad in blood-red garments, and having the peacock for his vehicle— may he protect us.

May Gaṇapati, the bestower of all goals, protect us— he whose crimson frontal globes are intoxicated with the thick flow of vermilion, who bears the splendor of a body like a dense rain-cloud, and who holds a supreme axe, a sweetmeat, and a rosary.
39b) Mālaka is the destruction of the sequence of oral tradition.
Seated upon the pericarp of a full-blown lotus, Śrī Siddhilakṣmī is as white as supreme camphor, crystal, the moon, and a conch;
she is the remover of all bonds and the perpetual burner of the mire of suffering in the ocean of saṃsāra. She is the ultimate liberation.
May she who possesses glorious five lotus-faces, ten arms, and stands upon a corpse protect us. 59.
May the Goddess, who bestows both supreme and lower accomplishments (*siddhi*), the mother of all mantras of incomparable power, extend them to us.
I bow to her, the Mother who is born from the *sraja* mantra, the abode of the highest light, the prosperity of accomplishment (*siddhilakṣmī*) that dwells within the hearts of the universe. 60.
O fulfiller of hopes, remover of sins, dispeller of the flood of the world's suffering, deliverer from afflictions, slayer of enemies, eternal dispeller of the delusion of saṃsāra;
O bringer of welfare, sovereign cause, you who do not move from the life-force of the best of lords— I [worship] you.
We praise Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, who bestows the most desired fruits immediately. || 61 ||
I bow to her who dwells most manifestly in the heart-lotus, having burst through the Brahma-knot; she who is mounted upon a mature corpse, endowed with ten arms, five faces, and three eyes;
who resides in the body as the *piṇḍasthā*, white as the moon, whose form consists of nectar, and who is both the creation and liberation of the universe.
The illustrious Siddhilakṣmī, who bestows desired fruits, assuming a massive form. || 62 ||
Mounted upon a lotus and a corpse, resembling a crystal gem, five-faced and three-eyed, she infatuates the three worlds; endowed with ten arms, her limbs are draped in divine garments;
in her left hands she carries a skull-cup, a trident, a jar, a boon-granting gesture, a great noose, and a severed head.
I bow to Siddhilakṣmī, who holds a bell, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a sword, and the gesture of fearlessness, together with an ear of grain. || 63 ||
She is Śrī Lakṣmī, whose union with every body is supreme bliss, born from the lotus, the crest-jewel among the jewels of women,
truly Mahālakṣmī, the great auspiciousness; she who holds power in her breasts, who pervades the three worlds, who binds the city of Laṅkā, and who bears the crescent digit of the waxing moon.
The Yoginī Śrī Kālikā is the essence of all qualities. 64.

I bow to the Goddess Jayasiddhilakṣmī, the bestower of boons, whose splendor is like the stainless moon rising from a beautiful seed; she whose lotus feet are revered with devotion by gods, asuras, and others, and who makes the essence of worldly devotion fruitful through her own lotus feet.
In the cremation ground of Navīra, which bestows all boons, she who is mounted upon Rudra out of love for the benefit of humble people—
may that primordial one, possessing ten arms and a face as radiant as the orb of the moon, grant me the glory of Śrī,
the fortune of spiritual perfection.

41a) Victorious is she who is intent on the arising of speech, who grants the fulfillment of all desires, who is the supreme boat for the ocean of saṃsāra, the auspicious destroyer of all afflictions;
she who, held by Śrī Sarveṇa, resides within the circle of the lotus, bestowing bliss and spiritual accomplishments— she is this very one.
The supreme Śrīsiddhilakṣmī is the stainless one whose mind is filled with glorious compassion. 67.
Beyond the seed-syllable of Māyā, she is the Supreme Self, belonging to the Kula; she is Mālinī composed of Māyā, the Great Goddess of the Mothers who brings joy;
she possesses the luster of a string of pearls within the Maṇi-kula;
she bestows the perfection of Māyā upon the minds of the wise, and she is the ordainer of the establishment of Yoga in the hearts of those possessed of pride.
By her grace, she bestows the attainment of all desired goals upon one who is intent on the propitiation of the mantra. 68.

Maṃ! She is the stainless forehead-moon of the illustrious Lord Śiva, the bestower of fortune, desire, and peace; the soul of the universe, the full mother of all beings, whose nature consists of the states of waking and so forth.
(41b) She sprinkles the three worlds with the nectar-water of her compassion, [overcoming] the fivefold states of death and time.
The supreme Śrī Siddhilakṣmī is victorious. 69.

From the syllable *kṣauṃ*, she arises as the destroyer of floods of evil; she who causes the fulfillment of all tasks—whether performed by herself, caused to be done, or even approved—with various means such as thought and wealth; she who, through wisdom, burns away that which is born of ignorance;
she who possesses a banner of glorious compassion ever-blazing; she whose supreme self is wisdom; she is Śrī Siddhi.
The supreme, most excellent Bhagavatī is eternal and ever-present.
The Supreme Goddess, who dwells within the cycle of transmigration, emits the sound *kroṃ* through the organs of action, the hands, and the eyes;
she is endowed with the crescent moon and the sky, and through her crest-lock, she attains the state of Nāda from the primordial Sound (Anāda).
She is eternal, beyond objects, and infinite; the bestower of boons, she is both existence and non-existence, the sovereign of all qualities such as omniscience and the rest.
Victorious is Mantreśvarī Mātṛkā! || 71 ||

Seated upon Rudra, the mother of both the transcendent and the immanent, she is Śrī Siddhilakṣmī; she is the supreme moon with manifold radiance, the maker of brilliant light, the bestower of perfection, and the one who bestows wealth.
Bearing beauty and weapons, adorned with ornaments, the source of all auspiciousness, she is this very one whose nature is the universe.
I, the Goddess Śrī Karuṇāmaya, having served you, shall remember you.

From the secret place up to the aperture of Brahmā, the Lord of the abode of Kula manifests His body as the garland of seed-syllables rich with strings of beads— the mantra-syllables— along with the limbs and their constituent parts;
having become the very essence on the ground of reality, He abides in the state of equanimity at the end of the sixteen.
May the splendor of the Queen of Wisdom, the goddess of accomplishment, radiate forth for the attainment of the supreme state. 73.

I bow to you, who possess the splendor of ten million moons, whose radiating rays agitate the three worlds; whose majesty and power are upheld even by Rudra; who have pervaded the abode of the universe; who effect the maintenance, creation, and destruction of worldly existence; and who blaze with intense brilliance.
I [worship] Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, whose face is pure with three eyes. || 74 ||
Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Siddhilakṣmī.
Whatever merit exists in the four Vedas, that is established in these three words; the fruit of the horse sacrifice and other rites has been proclaimed by Tumburu. (75)
The sin accumulated over seven lifetimes is consumed in an instant by the mere utterance of [the name] Kūrca;
by the utterance of Prāsāda, one instantly becomes the very embodiment of Rudra.
By the mere utterance of Rāva, the accomplishment of the command (ājñāsiddhi) will certainly occur;
by the utterance of Saṃvarta, the pacification of untimely death (akālakāla) will certainly occur.
By the power of the goad, the life-force of all living beings arises;
by its prohibition, O Great Goddess, no hater of it exists.
By reciting "dviraṇḍāccāraṇe devī," one shall obtain victory in dispute;
having joined them together as one, one should mutter [the mantra] consisting of the number of letters in the name of Bhavānī.
O Goddess, the fruit of his merit cannot indeed be calculated, he who,
preceded by the observances of a woman, should cause [the mantra] to be recited one hundred thousand times.
There is no doubt that one becomes the Lord Bhairava; the perfection of the command (ājñāsiddhi) will certainly come to pass.
His haters perish like a mass of straw consumed by fire. || 81 ||
At night, one should recite the mantra preceded by offerings and oblations; then the power of the command will surely be attained within a single year, without a doubt. (82)
"Truth, truth, and again truth, O Daughter of the Mountain!
This supreme practice, which grants all desires, is declared to be the bringer of success through mere command. (83)
O beloved, perform with faith this practice of the accomplishment of time, which yields visible results, so that it may not be in vain or fruitless. 84.
43b) Or one may accomplish it upon a funeral pyre, or accomplish it with a corpse in an auspicious place;
O Goddess, one accomplishes even the impossible by offering an oblation at night. 85.
O lady of pure smiles, listen as I proclaim the sequence of this vidyā which grants the fulfillment of all commands; practice it always with unwavering faith. 86.
I perpetually bow to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, whose form is the syllable Oṃ, whose body is white as snow, who has five faces and fifteen long eyes, and who shines with ten lotus-hands. || 87 ||

I perpetually bow to Śrī Siddhilakṭhmī, who is well-established in the hearts of people in the form of the seed-syllable Hrīṃ, who causes them to dwell in the nature of bliss, and who is delightful with her ornaments of various jewels.

I perpetually bow to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, who shatters the pride of the Daityas with the sound of the syllable HŪṂ, whose feet are rubbed by the crest-jewels of Brahmā and Indra, who dwells within the body of Rudra, and who is adorned with a most beautiful attire. (89)

Hā! I perpetually bow to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, the sustainer of the universe, whose nature consists of the three qualities (guṇas), who is the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution; she is composed of light, and her heart is softened by compassion for the wretched. || 90 ||

I perpetually bow to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, who tears asunder the enemies of the gods in battle with the sounds of her *phreṃ* and *kāra* mantras; she of terrifying form to the mind, possessing a radiance equal to the thousand-rayed sun. || 91 ||

I perpetually bow to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, who agitates the pride of gods and demons, who is a daughter of the lord of nāgas, rich in fresh youth, and brilliantly radiant with weapons such as the sword. 92.

I perpetually bow to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, whose form is passion, who possesses the orb of the three worlds as her lower lip, whose beautiful teeth are ever-smiling, and whose breasts are like fresh clouds. || 93 ||

I perpetually bow down to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, who resembles the consort of the king of gods, who is pleased by devotion, who destroys the fear of worldly existence, who is beautiful in the three worlds, and who is worshipped by the hosts of deities. 94.

I perpetually bow to Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, the sole abode of liberation, the eye of the hosts of immortals, the root of bliss, enriched by the foremost of gods, and residing within the lotus-heart of all embodied beings.
This most secret hymn to Siddhilakṣmī, which has issued forth from the lotus-mouths of Hari, Hara, and others, is radiant.
By means of the kings of mantras,
even a mortal whose wealth is exhausted, if he recites them constantly on earth, becomes a lord of men,
served by all the sovereigns of kings. 96.
Thus ends the hymn of the nine syllables in the Mahārāva Tantra.

I bow to her who is the supreme state, cultivated through her own inherent nature, whose radiant form arises from the cavity of the fire of peace (śāntikāgni), who stands in the midst of the three paths of the moon, sun, and fire, and in whom the non-consciousness known as the objects of consciousness has dissolved.
Kālī || 97 ||

May this Tripura, who holds the splendor of Indra’s very bow upon her forehead, who possesses the beauty of the cool-rayed moon extending everywhere from her head—she who, like the light of the sun, ever dwells within the heart as a burning flame—cut through our bonds. aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ. May she sever us [from bondage].
By three steps taken with force, she became today composed of light and composed of speech. 98.
